about: Windows protections Rig may turn off for a while, and how. A `protection` step names one row by `id` and how long (`revertAfter`, minutes). There is no script text anywhere: the helper's own code reads, lowers and raises each row by its `kind` (helper/RigHelper/Protection.cs), and the same file is built into the helper.

Before a row is lowered, Rig's background service notes that it must come back on (helper/RigHelper/Reverts.cs). When the time is up the service raises it, reads it back and logs it, also after a restart. The service only ever raises.

`how` says in plain words what the code does. `kind` firewall uses Windows Firewall's own interface (HNetCfg.FwPolicy2) for one `profile`; defenderRealtime uses Defender's own settings class (MSFT_MpPreference) and reads MSFT_MpComputerStatus; registry writes one text value, `off` to lower and `on[0]` to raise, and counts any `on` value or none as on.
`policy` is a place that, when set, means an organisation owns the setting: the row is refused there.
`never` rows are never lowered by anything Rig does.

rows.name: Windows Firewall on public networks
rows.risk: Other devices on a public network, like a cafe's or an airport's Wi-Fi, can reach this PC while it is off.

how.lower: Sets FirewallEnabled for the Public profile to off.
how.raise: Sets FirewallEnabled for the Public profile to on.

rows.name: Windows Firewall on private networks
rows.risk: Other devices on your home or work network can reach this PC while it is off.

how.lower: Sets FirewallEnabled for the Private profile to off.
how.raise: Sets FirewallEnabled for the Private profile to on.

rows.name: Windows Firewall on domain networks
rows.risk: Other devices on your organisation's network can reach this PC while it is off.

how.lower: Sets FirewallEnabled for the Domain profile to off.
how.raise: Sets FirewallEnabled for the Domain profile to on.

rows.name: Microsoft Defender real-time protection
rows.risk: Files you open, download or install aren't checked for viruses while it is off.

how.lower: Sets DisableRealtimeMonitoring to true through MSFT_MpPreference. Refused while Tamper Protection is on, because Windows would ignore it.
how.raise: Sets DisableRealtimeMonitoring to false through MSFT_MpPreference.

rows.name: SmartScreen for apps and files
rows.risk: Windows doesn't warn before an unrecognised app or download runs while it is off.

how.read: The SmartScreenEnabled value; anything but Off is on.
how.raise: Sets SmartScreenEnabled back to what it was (Warn when Rig can't tell).

never.name: User Account Control
never.says: Rig never lowers User Account Control. Windows' own prompt is how you approve Rig's changes, so Rig leaves it alone

words.unknown: Rig doesn't turn that protection off. It can turn off, for a while
words.revertAfter: Rig turns a protection off for 15 minutes, 1 hour or 4 hours, then turns it back on
words.tier: It turns off a Windows protection for a while. Rig's background service turns it back on by itself when the time is up, even after a restart or with Rig closed
words.keep: It stops Rig from turning this protection back on by itself. It stays off until you turn it back on
words.keepOnlyYou: Only you can choose to keep a protection off, with the Keep it off button in the Rig app
